subject: Alphanumeric literals
notes: cite.py --check 8.3.3.2.3 "Character-1 may be any character in the coded character set" OK. STR_BODY admits every code point except the delimiter (undoubled) and CR/LF (which end the line, so cannot be literal content in any reference format); the compile-time alphanumeric set is UTF-16 (project charset decision), so nothing the source set can carry is refused. Probe p11: e-acute and a CJK ideograph in a Format 1 literal compile and round-trip. NOTE 1's UTF-8/mixed option is permissive ('neither required ... nor prohibited') and not provided. No spec-derived golden pins non-ASCII Format 1 content -> test-ref empty. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2014, 2023 (Annex E itemizes the 2014->2023 delta and lists no change to 8.3.3.2, so the rule stands in both; the 1985/2002 edge is NOT derivable in-repo -- no 2002 or 1985 text is held)
